title: Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch
statement:
A cafeteria has exactly as many sandwiches as students waiting in line. Every sandwich is either circular (`0`) or square (`1`), and every student wants one of those two types. `students[j]` is the wish of the student `j` places from the front of the line, and `sandwiches[i]` is the type of the sandwich `i` places from the top of a stack, so `sandwiches[0]` is on top.

The following step repeats: the student at the front looks at the top sandwich; if it is the type they want, they take it and leave the line, and otherwise they go to the back of the line. Serving stops once the line is empty or nobody still in the line wants the sandwich on top. Return the number of students who end up without lunch.
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating the line works, but notice what the rotation really does: a student who refuses just goes to the back, so the line keeps cycling until someone who wants the top sandwich reaches the front. The top sandwich is therefore taken if and only if at least one remaining student wants its type, and which student takes it does not matter. Only the number of students wanting each type counts. As soon as the top sandwich's type has no takers, nothing can ever change again, and every sandwich still in the stack, one per remaining student, goes uneaten.

## Approach

1. Count the students who want each type in `count[0]` and `count[1]`.
2. Go through the stack from the top with index `i`, reading the type `top`.
3. If nobody left wants `top`, serving is stuck: the `sandwiches.length - i` students still in line go hungry.
4. Otherwise one of them takes it, so decrease `count[top]`.
5. If the whole stack is served, return `0`.

## Example 1, step by step

`students = [1, 1, 0, 0]` gives `count = [2, 2]`. Sandwich `0` is taken, leaving `[1, 2]`; sandwich `1` leaves `[1, 1]`; sandwich `0` leaves `[0, 1]`; sandwich `1` leaves `[0, 0]`. Every sandwich found a taker, so the answer is `0`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count and one pass over the stack.
- Space: O(1): just two counters.

## Pitfalls

- Stopping a simulation after one refusal is wrong; it ends only when every student in the line refuses the same top sandwich.
- The answer is the number of sandwiches left, `sandwiches.length - i`, which equals the students left because one of each leaves together.
- Square sandwiches lower in the stack do not help: in Example 2 the three students left all want `1` and two `1` sandwiches remain, but a `0` sits on top and blocks them.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count[t]` | students still in line who want type `t` |
| `wish` | the type one student wants |
| `i` | index of the sandwich on top of the stack |
| `top` | that sandwich's type |

narration.2: Only how many students want each type matters, not their order in line.
narration.7: Serve the stack from the top down.
narration.8: This is the sandwich currently on top.
narration.9: If no one left wants this type, the line cycles forever without anyone taking it.
narration.10: Serving stops; one student is left for each sandwich still in the stack.
narration.12: Someone wants it; the rotation brings them to the front and they leave with it.
narration.14: Every sandwich was taken, so every student ate.
